question: What is the main focus of rural environmental health in maternal care?

options.A: Urban planning strategies for large Nigerian cities
options.B: The commercial production of synthetic fertilizers
options.C: Factors in the surroundings that influence health outcomes
options.D: The treatment of infectious diseases inside urban hospitals

explanation: Rural environmental health looks at the physical, chemical, and biological surroundings where villagers live and work, which directly impacts maternal wellness. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why should a rural midwife care about the environmental conditions of a pregnant woman's home?

options.A: Environmental factors have no real impact until after delivery
options.B: Home surroundings directly affect the health of the mother and unborn child
options.C: Midwives are legally required to inspect building foundations
options.D: Good housing guarantees an entirely pain-free labor process

explanation: Conditions like housing quality, water access, and air quality play a massive role in preventing complications during pregnancy and the newborn period. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is a key benefit of having cement floors instead of bare earth in a rural home?

options.A: They are much easier to keep clean and reduce parasite transmission
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any roof repairs
options.C: They automatically lower the local atmospheric temperature
options.D: They guarantee that the household will never experience malaria

explanation: Cement or plastered floors prevent dust accumulation and harbor fewer parasites and insects compared to bare earth floors. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h2)

question: What primary health problem does good perimeter drainage around a rural house help prevent?

options.B: Excessive indoor smoke from cooking fires
options.C: Stagnant water accumulation that breeds mosquitoes
options.D: Sudden electrical surges during heavy rainfall

explanation: Good drainage stops water from pooling near the foundation, which directly cuts down mosquito breeding sites and lowers malaria risk. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary health hazard of using open biomass fires inside poorly ventilated rural kitchens?

options.A: Sudden loss of hearing in newborn babies
options.C: Severe bone softening in adult women
options.D: Inhalation of dangerous smoke and carbon monoxide

explanation: Burning wood or charcoal indoors without proper ventilation fills the air with harmful soot and gases that damage the lungs. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h3)

question: How does cross-ventilation help improve indoor air quality in a rural home?

options.A: It lowers the humidity so much that cooking becomes unnecessary
options.B: It filters out all bacteria using natural window screens
options.C: It allows fresh outdoor air to push out trapped smoke and stale air
options.D: It cools the food faster before it is served to children

explanation: Opposing openings create a continuous breeze that clears away indoor pollutants and brings in clean oxygen. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common occupational hazard for pregnant farmers in rural communities?

options.A: Heavy physical lifting and long hours in the sun
options.B: Exposure to agricultural chemicals and pesticides
options.D: Risks of animal bites and zoonotic infections

explanation: Rural farmers work outdoors in agriculture, not in offices with computers, making strain injuries from office equipment irrelevant to their setting. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women particularly vulnerable when handling agricultural pesticides without protective gear?

options.A: Chemicals can cross into the body and harm the developing fetus
options.B: Agrochemicals make the skin too dark for routine checks
options.C: Pesticides instantly cause complete hearing loss in adults
options.D: Exposure prevents the mother from producing breastmilk later

explanation: Toxic agricultural chemicals can be absorbed through the skin or inhaled, posing serious risks of birth defects or pregnancy loss. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is a simple way to prevent hookworm infection and foot injuries among rural farmers?

options.A: Avoiding all contact with sunlight after midday
options.B: Applying perfumed oils to the legs every morning
options.C: Drinking boiled water before going to the farm
options.D: Wearing sturdy protective boots during farm work

explanation: Hookworm larvae live in damp soil and penetrate bare skin; wearing boots effectively blocks direct contact. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant farmer complains of back pain from working bent over all day. What practical adjustment should you suggest?

options.A: Carry heavier loads to strengthen back muscles
options.B: Use long-handled tools to reduce awkward bending
options.C: Stop drinking water entirely during farm hours
options.D: Switch immediately to night-time farming only

explanation: Long-handled farming tools allow the worker to maintain a more upright posture, easing strain on the pregnant spine. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why should a rural midwife collaborate with village leaders and local councils?

options.A: To construct new commercial buildings in the market square
options.B: To build community support for better environmental health policies
options.C: To take over local political leadership positions in the region
options.D: To collect taxes from local farmers on behalf of the clinic

explanation: Partnering with local leadership helps mobilize the community to improve housing, sanitation, and overall environmental health standards. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h6)

question: How do home visits help a midwife improve maternal health outcomes in a village?

options.A: They force villagers to build modern concrete houses instantly
options.B: They allow the midwife to spot environmental hazards unique to that family
options.C: They replace the need for any laboratory tests at the health facility
options.D: They guarantee that the family will receive financial grants

explanation: Seeing where patients live and work reveals specific dangers like indoor smoke or unsafe water storage that clinic talks might miss. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T4#BMP117_U4_T4_h6)
